questions.question: If you study hard, you ______ the examination.
questions.explanation: Type 1 Condition (Open): If + Simple Present (study) -> will + bare infinitive (will pass).

questions.question: If it rains, we ______ at home.
questions.explanation: Type 1 Condition: If + Present Simple (rains) -> will + V1 (will stay).

questions.question: If you heat ice, it ______ into water.
questions.explanation: Zero Condition (Universal Scientific Fact): If + Present Simple -> Present Simple (turns).

questions.question: If I won a lottery, I ______ a luxury house.
questions.explanation: Type 2 Condition (Hypothetical Present): If + Simple Past (won) -> would + bare infinitive (would buy).

questions.question: If I were the Prime Minister, I ______ corruption.
questions.explanation: Type 2 Subjunctive: If + were -> would + V1 (would eradicate).

questions.question: If she had invited me, I ______ the party.
questions.explanation: Type 3 Condition (Unfulfilled Past): If + Past Perfect (had invited) -> would have + V3 (would have attended).

questions.question: If they had played well, they ______ the match.
questions.explanation: Type 3: If + had played -> would have won.

questions.question: Had I known the truth, I ______ you.
questions.explanation: Inversion of Type 3: 'Had I known' = 'If I had known' -> would have told.

questions.question: Were I a bird, I ______ in the sky.
questions.explanation: Inversion of Type 2: 'Were I a bird' = 'If I were a bird' -> would fly.

questions.question: Should you meet him, ______ him my regards.
questions.explanation: Inversion of Type 1: 'Should you meet him' = 'If you happen to meet him' -> imperative 'give'.

questions.question: Unless you work hard, you ______ succeed.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' = 'If not'. 'Unless you work hard, you cannot succeed'.

questions.question: If he ______ faster, he would catch the bus.
questions.explanation: Type 2 requires Simple Past 'ran' when main clause has 'would catch'.

questions.question: If she ______ rich, she would help the poor.
questions.explanation: In hypothetical conditional clauses, 'were' is used with all persons (subjunctive mood).

questions.question: If I ______ you, I would not accept the offer.
questions.explanation: Idiomatic subjunctive advice: 'If I were you, I would...'.

questions.question: If you had taken an umbrella, you ______ wet.
questions.explanation: Type 3: If + had taken -> would not have got.

questions.question: If he had worked hard, he ______.
questions.explanation: Type 3: If + had worked -> would have passed.

questions.question: If you drop the glass, it ______.
questions.explanation: Zero/Type 1 Condition: Present simple cause and effect -> breaks.

questions.question: If I find your lost key, I ______ you.
What ______ you do if you missed the train?
questions.explanation: Type 2 question: If + missed (past) -> would you do?

questions.question: What would have happened if the driver ______ the brakes?
questions.explanation: Type 3 condition requires past perfect 'had not applied' after 'if'.

questions.question: If she came early, we ______ together.
questions.explanation: Type 2: If + came (past simple) -> could/would + V1.

questions.question: If water reaches 100 degrees Celsius, it ______.
Unless he ______ an apology, I will not forgive him.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' clause takes simple present 'tenders' for future conditions; no 'will' inside conditional clause.

questions.question: If you boil water, it ______ into steam.
questions.explanation: Zero condition: universal physical fact -> evaporates.

questions.question: If I had seen you, I ______ hello.
questions.explanation: Type 3: If + had seen -> would have said.

questions.question: Had he arrived on time, he ______ the speech.
questions.explanation: Inversion of Type 3: Had he arrived -> would have heard.

questions.question: If you ______ red and blue, you get purple.
If she ______ the truth, she would have been praised.
questions.explanation: Main clause has 'would have been', so 'if' clause requires past perfect 'had told'.

questions.question: I will phone you if I ______ any news.
questions.explanation: Time/conditional clause after 'if' takes present simple 'get'.

questions.question: If it ______ tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.
questions.explanation: Conditional clause takes present tense 'rains', not 'will rain'.

questions.question: If he ______ hard, he will win the prize.
If I had a car, I ______ you a lift.
questions.explanation: Type 2: 'had' is simple past here (possession), taking 'would give'.

questions.question: If she had enough money, she ______ a new laptop.
questions.explanation: Type 2: 'had' is simple past, taking 'would buy'.

questions.question: If they invited us, we ______.
Had she asked me, I ______ her.
questions.explanation: Inverted Type 3: Had she asked -> would have helped.

questions.question: Were he honest, people ______ him.
questions.explanation: Inverted Type 2: Were he honest -> would trust.

questions.question: If you ______ your homework, teacher will scold you.
If he ______ well, he would not have failed.
questions.explanation: Type 3: had prepared -> would not have failed.

questions.question: If I knew his address, I ______ him a letter.
If you touch a live wire, you ______ an electric shock.
If I had known you were in hospital, I ______ you.
questions.explanation: Type 3: had known -> would have visited.

questions.question: If the sun shines, the snow ______.
If she practice regularly, she ______ fluent in English.
Had the police arrived in time, the robbery ______.
questions.explanation: Type 3 passive: Had the police arrived -> would have been averted.

questions.question: Were I in your place, I ______ that job.
questions.explanation: Type 2 subjunctive: Were I in your place -> would reject.

questions.question: If you ______ green and yellow, you get cyan.
If he had taken medicine, he ______ better now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: Past condition (had taken) with present result (now) -> would feel.

questions.question: If they ______ the flight, they would have been stranded.
questions.explanation: Type 3: had missed -> would have been.

questions.question: Unless you ______ immediately, you will be late.
If I were an eagle, I ______ above the clouds.
If you press this button, the alarm ______.
If he ______ careful, he would not have met with an accident.
questions.explanation: Type 3: had been -> would not have met.

questions.question: If you don't water plants, they ______.
If she ______ the competition, she will get a scholarship.
If I had known his real intention, I ______ him.
questions.explanation: Type 3: had known -> would not have trusted.

questions.question: Were the weather fine, we ______ for a picnic.
questions.explanation: Inversion Type 2: Were the weather fine -> would go.

questions.question: Had we left earlier, we ______ caught the train.
questions.explanation: Type 3: Had we left -> would have caught.

questions.question: If you ______ milk, it turns into curd.
If she ______ harder, she would speak English fluently.
If I ______ ten million dollars, I would build a hospital.
What ______ you have done if you had been in my position?
questions.explanation: Type 3 question: What would you have done if...

questions.question: If you heat water, it ______ at 100°C.
Had I realized the danger, I ______ entered the cave.
questions.explanation: Inverted Type 3: would not have entered.

questions.question: If he ______ the truth, he would not be in trouble now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: past action (had told) affecting present state.

questions.question: If you ______ oil on water, it floats.
Unless she ______ hard, she will not pass.
questions.explanation: Present simple inside unless clause: works.

questions.question: If I ______ you, I would consult a lawyer.
If they ______ the signal, the accident wouldn't have happened.
questions.explanation: Type 3: hadn't ignored -> wouldn't have happened.

questions.question: If you freeze water, it ______ ice.
If she ______ earlier, she wouldn't have missed the bus.
questions.explanation: Type 3: had started -> wouldn't have missed.

questions.question: Were she here, she ______ support us.
questions.explanation: Inverted Type 2: Were she here -> would support.

questions.question: Had you told me earlier, I ______ arranged the tickets.
questions.explanation: Type 3 with modal: could have arranged.

questions.question: If I ______ wings, I would fly across the world.
If you ______ late, you will miss the keynote speech.
If he ______ the money, he would have repaid the debt.
questions.explanation: Type 3 requires Past Perfect: had (auxiliary) + had (V3) -> had had.

questions.question: If it ______ heavily, the match will be abandoned.
